requirement: The core (source, schemas, vocabularies, error codes, messages and its own tests) contains no domain-specific term. Domain meaning lives only in packs. A static check over the core enforces this against a versioned deny-list and must be shown to fail on a planted term.
The core depends on no APG module, no pack and no consumer. Dependency direction is pack -> core (a pack is data that the core validates), and consumer -> core. A static import check enforces it.

The core publishes, through describe(), its core version, pack-schema version, signal-vocabulary version, outcome-vocabulary version, event-class vocabulary version and error-vocabulary version. Every result pins all of them.

The core is deterministic: it reads no wall clock, random source, network, file system or environment. Every time value is an input (evaluation_date, as_of, retrieved_at). The same inputs always give the same bytes.

A subject is an opaque pack-scoped identifier with a pack-declared kind. Equivalence between identifiers exists only where the pack declares it in an explicit table. The core never infers equivalence; an alias that maps to more than one canonical identifier, or a cycle, makes the pack invalid. Values are compared only within one unit, one market and one pack-declared comparison group.

An observation carries: source_id, licence_ref, market, unit, observation_class, value_basis, as_of date and retrieved_at, plus its value (LEVEL) or its event class (EVENT). An observation missing any required attribute, or naming a source, licence, unit, market or class the pack does not declare, is rejected with the field named and is counted as rejected; it is never used.

Numeric values are signed integers with an explicit decimal exponent. Floats, NaN, infinities, booleans and numeric strings are refused. Ratios are exact integer fractions; no floating-point arithmetic is used anywhere in the core. Zero is a value only when observed; absence is never zero. Whether a value of a unit may be zero or negative is decided per unit by the pack (MIE-R-64); the core never assumes that a value is a positive price.

observation_class is one of HISTORICAL_MOVEMENT, CURRENT_REFERENCE or COUNTERPARTY_OFFER; forward scenarios are caller inputs, never stored observations (MIE-R-25), and are the fourth evidence group. value_basis is one of ASKING, OFFER, INDEX, COMPLETED_TRANSACTION. Class and basis are kept on every evidence item and are never merged, averaged across or relabelled.

Licence gate: an observation is stored only when its licence_ref resolves in the pack to status LICENSED at ingestion, and it is used only while the licence is LICENSED and within its validity window at the evaluation_date. UNLICENSED, UNKNOWN and EXPIRED are never used, and an unknown status is never treated as licensed. The core evaluates only status and window; it never interprets licence terms.

Time rules: an observation dated after the evaluation_date is never used, however recent its retrieval; retrieved_at earlier than as_of is refused; an observation whose valid_until is before the evaluation_date is EXPIRED for current use and remains usable only as labelled history.

No gap filling: the core performs no interpolation, extrapolation, smoothing, carry-forward or borrowing from other series or from the future. A missing point stays missing and is reported as an evidence gap.

Conflicts: two different values for one series and as_of with the same revision are both reported and the date is listed as conflicting; the core never chooses between them. A higher source revision supersedes a lower one. An exact repeat is one observation. A signal that would use a conflicting point is NOT_ASSESSED with reason CONFLICT_IN_EVIDENCE.

Observations are append-only and content-addressed (id = digest of canonical bytes). Re-submission is an idempotent no-op. A correction is a new observation that supersedes the old one; the old one is retained for replay.

Freshness is explicit and has no default. A freshness limit (whole calendar days) comes from the pack (owner-supplied configuration) or the request. A missing, null, boolean, float or negative limit gives NOT_ASSESSED with reason FRESHNESS_LIMIT_MISSING for that evidence. Exactly at the limit is fresh; one day past is stale. The limit and the data age are recorded in the result.

The signal vocabulary is closed and versioned (mie-signal-1: LEVEL_MOVEMENT, CONVERSION_MOVEMENT, AVAILABILITY_CHANGE, VARIANT_INTRODUCED, VARIANT_WITHDRAWN, DATA_STALE, DATA_MISSING, DATA_CONFLICT). A pack chooses which signals apply and supplies their parameters; it cannot add a signal type or change a type's meaning. A change to the vocabulary is a core change with a new vocabulary version.

A signal reports an observed fact about evidence. No signal, field or message states or implies a future price or a prediction. The schema contains no field named forecast, predicted, expected or projected (enforced by a static check).

Every signal carries: type, vocabulary version, status (ASSESSED or NOT_ASSESSED with reason), subject, class and basis of its evidence, window, evidence identifiers, data age, the parameters used and their source, and a structured basis statement (counts of observations, distinct sources, conflicts and gaps). A movement signal also carries its movement basis, the endpoint values, the exact difference, the exact ratio where defined, the direction and the crosses_zero flag (MIE-R-65). The basis statement is descriptive; it is not a probability and invents no confidence number.

Signal parameters (window length, minimum points, movement threshold as an integer ratio, freshness limits and similar) have no defaults. A missing parameter gives NOT_ASSESSED with reason PARAMETER_MISSING for that signal. The builder ships no parameter value in any production pack; any value used in a test is a test fixture flagged TEST-ONLY.
Results keep four evidence groups apart and never merge them: historical movement, current reference, counterparty-offer movement and forward scenarios.

Direction neutrality: the core contains no rule, bias or default that assumes levels will rise or fall. Given mirrored histories the core produces mirrored signals and no outcome preference arises from the core.

A pack declares its allowed intentions (subset of BUY, SELL). The outcome vocabulary is fixed per intention: BUY gives ACT_NOW, WAIT, STAGE, NEGOTIATE or NOT_ASSESSED; SELL gives ACT_NOW, HOLD, WAIT or NOT_ASSESSED. An intention the pack does not allow is refused with INTENTION_NOT_ALLOWED, and no code path can emit an outcome outside the pack's allowed intentions.

Outcomes are chosen only by the pack's decision table: ordered rules, a closed predicate language (signal present or not assessed, gap present, constraint comparison against a pack parameter, scenario present, qualification), first match wins. The core ships no rules. No table gives NOT_ASSESSED/NO_TABLE; no matching rule gives NOT_ASSESSED/NO_RULE_MATCHED. Any rule that uses a market-signal predicate, and any rule placed after one (a downstream rule), is governed by the signal-influence safeguard of MIE-R-63 whatever its configured outcome, NOT_ASSESSED included (v0.1 restricted the owner-assumption requirement to WAIT and HOLD; v0.2 extended it to every outcome of a signal-influenced rule but exempted later rules after a signal-influenced NOT_ASSESSED rule; v0.3 removes that exemption).

Every timing result discloses: the evidence used (by identifier, class and basis), data ages and freshness limits, the rule fired, the constraints echoed, an uncertainty statement derived from the basis counts, all evidence gaps, the qualification (UNQUALIFIED or QUALIFIED with reasons), the signal-influence class (MIE-R-63) and the assumption label where one applies.

Every missing, excluded, stale, conflicting or unlicensed input appears as an evidence gap with a reason code. A gap is never counted as zero and never silently dropped. When evidence a fired rule depends on is absent, the result is NOT_ASSESSED or QUALIFIED as the rule table states, never a bare outcome.

Forward scenarios are explicit caller inputs (identifier, label, owner reference, basis statement, assumed level and unit). The core never generates a scenario, never derives one from history, labels each as an ASSUMPTION and not a forecast, and has no operation or message that reads, writes or references an approved forecast.
Results are advisory records. The service has no operation that places an order, commits a purchase or sale, sends a notification or changes external state. Every result states that a human decides.

Qualification: stale, expired, unavailable or conflicting current evidence makes the result QUALIFIED with the limitation stated. Stale or expired observations may remain historical evidence but never support an UNQUALIFIED current result.

A pack is data only: a closed schema (mie-pack-1) of vocabulary, units, markets, sources, licence records, equivalence tables, comparison groups, enabled signals with parameters, freshness limits, allowed intentions, decision table, lifecycle-event mapping, hook declarations and provenance. Unknown keys, executable content and duplicate keys are refused.

A pack is identified by pack_id, pack_version and a SHA-256 over its canonical bytes (canonical form defined in the specification). Every request pins the pack as (id, version, hash); a mismatch is refused with PACK_HASH_MISMATCH.

Published packs are immutable. (id, version) is bound to one hash forever; re-publishing identical bytes is an idempotent no-op; different bytes under the same (id, version) are refused with PACK_VERSION_CONFLICT. Withdrawal is a separate registry record: a withdrawn pack accepts no new assessments but its results still replay.

Pack validation refuses with a stated reason: malformed or unknown structure; attempts to override a core invariant (default freshness, treating a non-LICENSED status as usable, floats, intentions outside BUY/SELL, new signal types, changed signal meaning, outcomes outside the per-intention vocabulary); dangling references; duplicate identifiers; non-NFC text; and rules whose outcome is not allowed for their intention.
A pack declares the exact core versions it is compatible with. A pack naming an unsupported pack-schema version, or no core version the running core supports, is refused.

Activation for a tenant requires an owner approval reference supplied by the pack owner. The core records it and asks the host's ApprovalVerifierPort to verify it; the core cannot approve a pack, and a builder-authored pack cannot self-approve. Activation pins the hash; later activations never edit earlier ones.

Each pack declares a decision profile. CONTEXT_ONLY: market signals are returned as context beside the outcome, no rule may use a market-signal predicate, and the signal-influence class of every outcome is NONE. SIGNAL_RULES: rules may use market-signal predicates subject to MIE-R-63. The APG construction pack is CONTEXT_ONLY and unconnected until the product owner approves the Section 08 change request and chooses between its options.

Every result has an identifier derived from the canonical bytes of: core version and all vocabulary versions, pack (id, version, hash), the request, and the evidence set (observation ids with digests). Any change in any pinned input changes the identifier.

Replay recomputes a result from its pinned inputs using the stored evidence by identifier, never the latest data, and must reproduce the stored result byte for byte. Missing stored evidence gives REPLAY_EVIDENCE_UNAVAILABLE, never a partial replay.
Replaying under a different core or pack version produces a drift report listing every difference; the original result is never overwritten.

Every operation takes a tenant context verified by the host's TenantContextPort. The tenant is never read from a payload; a payload tenant field is refused. A missing, forged or expired context is refused for every operation.

Tenant isolation: another tenant's subject, series, observation, result or activation is indistinguishable from a missing one (same code, same shape). A licence held by one tenant is not a licence for another. Returned values are independent copies. Storage keys are tenant-scoped.

Every operation that has a verified tenant context, including refusals, yields an audit event through the host's AuditLogPort (identifiers and digests, never licensed values), sequenced as MIE-R-61 states. If the event cannot be recorded the operation fails closed with AUDIT_UNAVAILABLE: no result is returned and no state changes. A context that cannot be verified has no tenant to attribute an event to: that refusal returns the context error and produces no tenant audit event (MIE-OQ-24).

Any failure fails closed: a typed error from the error vocabulary, never a partial result and never an outcome. An unexpected exception becomes INTERNAL_ERROR_FAIL_CLOSED. Not-assessable evidence is reported through reason codes inside a complete result, never as a silent omission.

All sizes (batch size, string length, series length, rule count, pack size) are bounded by a limits object supplied by the host. The core ships no production limit value; absent limits give LIMIT_NOT_CONFIGURED and exceeded limits give LIMIT_EXCEEDED.
All text is treated as data: NFC-normalised or refused, control characters refused, bounded in length. Text in any field never alters behaviour (injection-like content is inert).

The service boundary is the set of operations in MIE1_PORTS.csv (OP-01..OP-12). Messages are value-typed canonical objects; each operation takes a verified tenant context. Each operation lists every error it can return, including the common failures of MIE-R-62. The semantics are identical whether the core is embedded as a library or hosted as a service; the specification commits to neither.

Everything the core needs from its host is an outbound port with a contract: TenantContextPort, ObservationStorePort, PackRegistryPort, ResultStorePort, AuditLogPort (append), AuditQueryPort (read and verify), CostValueHookPort, ApprovalVerifierPort, and a LimitsConfig object. ObservationSourcePort is NOT an outbound port of the core: it is an adapter-side contract between the ingestion side and a feed (MIE-R-66), and the core never calls it. No port assumes a database, queue, scheduler, vendor or deployment shape.

Each outbound port has a reference implementation (in-memory test double) and a contract suite, and so does the adapter-side ObservationSourcePort. Reference implementations are labelled non-production and make no persistence, durability or performance claim.

Observations derived from a MarketFeedPort-style feed enter the core only through submit_observations (OP-07), submitted from the ingestion side (MIE-R-66). The core's contract suite includes an analogue of each of MF-01..MF-13 applied at OP-07 and at assessment. The M6 MarketFeedPort definition is not changed; a mapping adapter on the ingestion side is the integration route.

Cost and value models (for example landed cost in one field, depreciation in another) are outside the core. The core defines a CostValueHookPort slot that a pack may declare by name, with a determinism contract and a test double. No hook implementation, formula or value is built or specified in MIE-1.
The APG construction pack allows BUY only. Its vocabulary references the M6 terms by name and does not redefine M6 behaviour. No SELL-side outcome can be produced under this pack (shown by test).

The APG pack contains no threshold, freshness limit, parameter, rule or financial assumption supplied by the builder. It is INCOMPLETE until the policy owner supplies them; an incomplete pack yields NOT_ASSESSED with the missing items listed.

Isolation gate: until the product owner separately approves the Section 08 change request, no market signal feeds any APG finding or recommendation. No APG module imports the core, no consumer adapter is wired, and APG outputs are byte-identical with and without the core present.
M6, the whole existing APG suite, locked Sections 00-18, CR-09, the RTM and every preserved release remain unchanged; the preserved hashes are re-verified.

The synthetic portability pack ("test field") is labelled SYNTHETIC, uses invented illustrative identifiers, allows BUY and SELL, names no vendor, uses no real data, makes no market claim, contains no luxury-specific functionality, and exists only to show that a second field plugs in. Its values are TEST-ONLY.
Portability: adding the synthetic pack requires no change to any core file (core file hashes identical before and after), and both packs run through the same core code path.

Test strategy covers unit, port-contract, adversarial, replay, tenancy, static (neutrality, import graph, forbidden fields, clock/network use), frozen-baseline and sabotage families, each with identified cases (MIE1_TEST_STRATEGY.csv).
Sabotage proof: every mutant in MIE1_SABOTAGE_CATALOGUE.csv is caught by at least one named test. A surviving mutant is a defect unless recorded as an equivalent mutant with a reason.
Reports separate builder-run results from independently verified results and give exact artifact hashes, defects and limitations.
No document or result claims production readiness, market validity, predictive power, comprehensive market coverage, or completeness beyond the authorised milestone.
The Section 08 change request is drafted as an unnumbered DRAFT for the product owner. It is not approved by the build and edits no locked file.

Audit read path. AuditLogPort (PT-05) offers append only. A separate AuditQueryPort (PT-10) offers read (tenant, from sequence, limit) and verify (tenant), tenant-scoped, read-only, returning copies. list_audit (OP-12) reads the calling tenant's events only through AuditQueryPort and returns them with the chain verification result and the cutoff sequence number. list_audit is itself audited (MIE-R-40) without recursion: it fixes the cutoff sequence number first, reads up to the cutoff, and then appends exactly one access event (event type AUDIT_READ); that event is not in its own result and returning it creates no further event; the next list_audit call shows it. If the access event cannot be appended, list_audit returns AUDIT_UNAVAILABLE and no events. A broken or tampered chain is reported by the verification result and is never trimmed or repaired. The core has no other route to read or write audit events.
basis: EDR-03; apg/ports.py:146-150; apg/contracts/audit_log_contract.py AL-03, AL-09; RUL-MIE-10; NEW

requirement: Audit sequencing and event outcomes. For an operation with a verified tenant context the core (1) validates the request, (2) computes the outcome without side effects, (3) appends the audit event, (4) only then commits state through the store ports, and (5) returns the result. If step 3 fails the operation returns AUDIT_UNAVAILABLE with no result and no state change. The event carries the operation identifier, an outcome class (OK for a completed read or validation, ACCEPTED for a state-changing operation that passed validation and is about to commit, REFUSED for a refusal, FAILED for a failure), the error code if any, a correlation identifier and digests. ACCEPTED is not proof that the commit happened: if a store port fails at step 4 the core returns STORE_UNAVAILABLE, makes one attempt to append a FAILED event, and the trail never records a completed state change that did not happen. Atomicity between an audit append and a store commit is a host property the core cannot supply (MIE-OQ-23, MIE-L-17).

Error-vocabulary completeness. MIE1_PORTS.csv lists, for each operation, every error it can return. Every operation lists the common failures TENANT_CONTEXT_MISSING, TENANT_CONTEXT_INVALID, AUDIT_UNAVAILABLE and INTERNAL_ERROR_FAIL_CLOSED. Every operation that takes input beyond the context lists REQUEST_MALFORMED; every operation that uses a store port lists STORE_UNAVAILABLE; every operation whose input size is bounded by limits lists LIMIT_NOT_CONFIGURED and LIMIT_EXCEEDED. The register and the specification must agree, and the checker enforces the lists.

Signal-influence safeguard for every outcome. A market signal is a signal of type LEVEL_MOVEMENT, CONVERSION_MOVEMENT, AVAILABILITY_CHANGE, VARIANT_INTRODUCED or VARIANT_WITHDRAWN; DATA_STALE, DATA_MISSING and DATA_CONFLICT are data-quality signals and are handled as gap and qualification predicates. Two structural definitions govern the pack check and the result class alike. (1) A rule is signal-influenced when it uses a market-signal predicate (SIGNAL_PRESENT or SIGNAL_NOT_ASSESSED on a market-signal type), whatever its configured outcome (ACT_NOW, WAIT, STAGE, NEGOTIATE, HOLD or NOT_ASSESSED). (2) A rule is downstream when at least one signal-influenced rule stands earlier in the table, whatever that earlier rule's configured outcome or basis class and whether or not the rule itself uses a market-signal predicate. Because the table is first-match, a downstream rule can fire only because every earlier rule, the signal-influenced ones included, did not match. Pack check: every signal-influenced rule and every downstream rule must carry basis_class OWNER_ASSUMPTION with an owner reference and an assumption statement, whatever its own configured outcome (NOT_ASSESSED included) and whatever the configured outcome of the earlier signal-influenced rule; otherwise the pack is refused with PACK_RULE_POLICY_VIOLATION by validate_pack and by register_pack, nothing is stored and the pack cannot be retrieved or activated. Equivalently, every rule from the first signal-influenced rule onward is owner-labelled; a pack that wants unassumed rules places them before the first signal-influenced rule, and a no-match outcome needs no rule (NO_RULE_MATCHED). Result class, by the same two definitions: DIRECT if the fired rule is signal-influenced; PRECEDENCE if the fired rule is downstream and is not itself signal-influenced; NONE if the fired rule is neither (no signal-influenced rule stands before it), if the profile is CONTEXT_ONLY, or if no rule fired (NOT_ASSESSED with reason NO_TABLE or NO_RULE_MATCHED; with NO_RULE_MATCHED the identifiers of the signal-influenced rules evaluated are listed). Because the pack check and the class use one definition, every result of class DIRECT or PRECEDENCE has a fired rule that is owner-labelled (MIE-R-69). A DIRECT or PRECEDENCE outcome is labelled assumption-based and carries the owner reference and assumption statement of the fired rule and the identifiers of the signal-influenced rules evaluated; it is never presented as a forecast or as a tendency of prices, and it is qualified when its evidence is stale, expired, unavailable or conflicting. A pack containing any OWNER_ASSUMPTION rule can be activated only with a verified approval reference (MIE-R-33), and the result records that reference. The core does not judge whether a signal is materially influential: influence is structural, so the label can over-state influence and cannot under-state it (MIE-L-19, MIE-OQ-26).

Value domains. Each unit in a pack declares value_domain: POSITIVE (value > 0), NON_NEGATIVE (value >= 0) or SIGNED (any integer). There is no default; a pack whose unit lacks it is refused with PACK_MALFORMED. An observation outside its unit's declared domain is rejected with OBSERVATION_INVALID, reason VALUE_OUT_OF_DOMAIN, and counted as rejected. A conversion series must be in the POSITIVE domain. The core never infers that a value is a price, and never infers zero.

Movement mathematics. For LEVEL_MOVEMENT and CONVERSION_MOVEMENT let s be the start value and e the end value, aligned to a common decimal exponent as exact integers, and d = e - s. The pack declares, with no default, a movement_basis (ABSOLUTE or RELATIVE) and a threshold T as an exact positive integer ratio p/q (a zero, negative or non-integer-ratio threshold refuses the pack). ABSOLUTE: defined for every s and e including zero and negative; T is a difference in the unit itself; direction is UP when d >= T, DOWN when d <= -T, otherwise UNCHANGED. RELATIVE: the ratio is r = d / |s|, using the absolute value of the start, so the sign of r is always the sign of d and a rise in value is UP for a negative start exactly as for a positive one; it is defined only when s is not zero, otherwise the signal is NOT_ASSESSED with reason ZERO_BASE and a gap is listed; direction is UP when r >= T, DOWN when r <= -T, otherwise UNCHANGED. When s and e have opposite signs the signal states crosses_zero = true, so that r is not read as a percentage change of a price. Every movement signal reports basis, s, e, d, r (when defined), direction and crosses_zero. Negating every value of a SIGNED series negates d and r and exchanges UP with DOWN under both bases (a tested property: MIE-R-20). No movement is computed with a signed denominator or with floating point. The core cannot judge whether a relative measure is meaningful for a given series; that is the pack owner's choice (MIE-L-20).

Observation-feed flow. Retrieval, mapping and scheduling are outside the core. (1) An ingestion driver on the host or integration side decides when to retrieve; the trigger is not specified and no scheduler or deployment is assumed. (2) The driver calls a feed adapter, which is the only component that invokes ObservationSourcePort and the only one that knows a feed's protocol. (3) The feed adapter maps what it retrieved to the observation message schema, setting source_id, licence_ref, market, unit, class, basis, as_of and retrieved_at. (4) The driver submits the mapped batch, with its verified tenant context and pack pin, to submit_observations (OP-07). (5) The core alone validates every item (attributes, pack declarations, licence gate, value domain, time rules, limits) and returns a per-item receipt; any validation the adapter performs is a convenience and is never trusted. (6) The driver acts on the receipts; a retry is safe because identical content is a duplicate no-op. The core never calls ObservationSourcePort or any feed, never retrieves during get_signals or assess_timing, and never learns of a feed failure: a feed failure is an adapter-side event, no core operation is invoked, and it reaches the core only as a missing observation, which is an evidence gap. A licence status asserted by a feed is recorded as evidence at most; only the pack's licence record grants use. retrieved_at is asserted by the adapter and the core checks only that it is not earlier than as_of (MIE-L-18). M6 and its MarketFeedPort are not changed, and which component runs the driver and the adapter, and where, is not decided (MIE-OQ-25).

Specification-approval dispositions. For each of MIE-OQ-05, -06, -10, -11, -14, -16, -18, -19 and -20, MIE1_OQ_DISPOSITIONS.csv records the disposition the specification is written to, its justification, its basis (the independent reviewer's recorded default where one exists, otherwise the builder's recommendation), the consequence of the alternative, the decision owner, the decision still needed and a status that is either SPECIFIED - REVIEWER CONFIRMATION REQUIRED or SPECIFIED AS PROPOSED - PRODUCT-OWNER DECISION REQUIRED. No disposition is recorded as decided by the builder, and no product-owner decision is made by this specification.

Revision discipline. A revision is additive: the earlier package is preserved unchanged, its ZIP hash is recorded and re-verified, and a change log maps every audit point to the requirements, acceptance criteria, tests, mutants and registers changed. Every register row added or revised in a revision is tagged.

Pack and result consistency. A pack that breaks MIE-R-63 produces no result of any class: validate_pack and register_pack refuse it with PACK_RULE_POLICY_VIOLATION, register_pack stores nothing, get_pack and activate_pack then return NOT_FOUND, and assess_timing against its pin returns PACK_NOT_ACTIVE. The evaluator also checks the fired rule before it emits a result: if a DIRECT or PRECEDENCE result would be produced from a rule that lacks basis_class OWNER_ASSUMPTION, an owner reference or an assumption statement, the core emits no outcome, returns INTERNAL_ERROR_FAIL_CLOSED, appends a FAILED audit event (MIE-R-61) and stores no result. An unlabelled DIRECT or PRECEDENCE result is therefore never emitted.

Explicit implementation blockers. MIE1_IMPLEMENTATION_BLOCKERS.csv records the conditions that must be met before implementation can be authorised: BLK-01 audit append and state commit are not atomic and need an explicit recorded design decision (MIE-R-61, MIE-L-17, MIE-OQ-23); BLK-02 the mapping from M6 observation attributes and kinds to the core is not derived (MIE-R-49, MIE-L-16); BLK-03 the cascade impact assessment of the Section 08 change is unfinished (MIE-R-59, MIE-L-21). Each is shown as open and blocking; none is marked resolved; the builder makes no decision on BLK-01; closing a blocker needs independent review. The product owner's decision on the Section 08 change request (Option A, Option B or neither) is separate and also outstanding (MIE-R-51).
